claims.text: Schwab's 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026, published October 15, 2026) states Schwab has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed: "We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that management believes Schwab can maintain its competitive position in RIA custody primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed: "Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients."

Trade press reported (October 28, 2026) that President and CEO Rick Wurster told an audience of advisors at Schwab Impact that "Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM."

Trade press reported (October 28, 2026) that Wurster said Schwab's role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps RIA firms support their clients and thrive: "Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive."

Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026) states Schwab's strategy includes being the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service: "The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service."

Trade press reported (October 29, 2026) that Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies.

Schwab's 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026, published August 7, 2026) describes its Advisor Services segment as providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers: "The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers."

Schwab's 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026, published October 15, 2026) states Schwab serves more than 16,000 RIA firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support: "we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that, as custodian, Schwab earns revenue from the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee: "By functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. In this capacity, we do not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that RIAs who custody client accounts at Schwab may use proprietary software for up-to-date client account information and trading, and that the Advisor Services website is the core platform for RIAs to conduct daily business activities online: "RIAs who custody client accounts at Schwab may use proprietary software that provides them with up-to-date client account information as well as trading capabilities. The Advisor Services website is the core platform for RIAs to conduct daily business activities online with Schwab."

Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026) describes Advisor Services as in a position of strength and a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2 trillion in client assets, 16,000 advisory firms, and 3.9 million households, and as #1 in RIA custodial assets: "Advisor Services is in a position of strength & remains a driving force for Schwab. $5.2T Client Assets 16K Advisory Firms Households 3.9M in RIA Custodial Assets #1."

Schwab's July 2026 monthly activity report (period ended July 31, 2026, published August 14, 2026) describes its offering to independent, fee-based investment advisors as custodial, operational and trading support through Schwab Advisor Services: "custodial, operational and trading support for independent, fee-based investment advisors through Schwab Advisor Services TM."

Schwab's 3Q25 transcript (period ended September 30, 2025, published October 16, 2025) states that in advisor services Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody, and has grown its lending support, alternatives capability, and institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform: "In our advisor services business, we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that Schwab focuses on superior service and uses technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

Trade press reported (October 29, 2026) that Wurster cited the growing use of pledged-asset lending balances, the demand for long-short investment strategies, and the need to make private-market investing more accessible to the masses as focus areas for Schwab's custody offerings.

Schwab's 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024, published January 21, 2025) states that in advisor services Schwab is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence: "In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that in the Advisor Services arena Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies: "In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies."
Trade press reported (October 29, 2026) that CEO Rick Wurster said independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have strong banks attached to their advice.

Schwab's 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025, published January 21, 2026) states that CEO Rick Wurster said RIAs do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses: "They do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses."

Schwab's 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026, published October 15, 2026) states that CEO Rick Wurster said, looking to October, Schwab changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent: "as we look to October, where we have changed the minimums for long/short and throttled growth to some extent, the growth has in no way slowed at all in terms of AS NNA."

Trade press reported (October 28, 2026) that Wurster said Schwab limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors: "That led the firm to limit long-short offerings only to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors."

Trade press reported (October 28, 2026) that Wurster said Schwab reduced the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM: "reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM."

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that during the Ameritrade integration Schwab experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs, though such attrition was below its initial estimates: "we experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs, though such attrition was below our initial estimates."
